title: Peptide ML prediction on the machine's own conda env

steps.why: the repo's own gate list (code/gates.json) - the same questions check_all.sh asks

bash-free python wrapper: git-bash exists on the machine but is not on PATH, so {bash} cannot be trusted there. run_peptide_ml.py re-discovers a qualifying interpreter (probe report + fresh scan of both layouts, first with numpy/pandas/sklearn wins) and runs the umami-peptide RandomForest: 300 train / 100 test, metrics + predictions.csv + self-assert accuracy>=0.80

note: Session 01a0ad15 round 40: the user asked for a peptide ML prediction using their local conda envs (round 39 probe: 13 envs, ml_ready=yes, best=AMPidentifier). The wrapper re-discovers a qualifying interpreter at runtime (no hard-coded env, no install). Training data is SYNTHETIC DEMO (seeded, known rule) - a functional test; replace build_dataset() with a real CSV reader for real data.
